title: HELIX Terminology: Compensation Type
description: Types of compensation components in higher education institutions.

codes.definition: Primary annual or academic-year salary for the position. For 9-month faculty, this is the academic year (AY) base; for 12-month staff, this is the fiscal year (FY) base.
Compensation calculated per hour worked. Used for non-exempt staff, student workers, temporary employees. Subject to FLSA minimum wage and overtime rules.
Fixed payment for a specific role or responsibility, not tied to hours worked. Examples: department chair stipend, graduate assistant stipend, coaching stipend, program director stipend.

Additional compensation for teaching or duties beyond the standard workload. Faculty teaching above their contractual load (e.g., 4/4 teaching 5/4) receive overload pay, typically calculated per credit hour.

Compensation for 9-month faculty working during summer term. Typically capped at a fraction of base salary (often 2/9 or 3/9 of AY salary). May be funded from grants, instruction, or administrative budgets.
Temporary salary increase for faculty or staff taking on additional administrative duties. Examples: interim dean, accreditation coordinator, assessment director. Removed when duties end.
Temporary pay increase for an individual formally appointed to act in a higher-level position during a vacancy or leave. Governed by institutional acting appointment policy.

Additional compensation for working non-standard shifts (evening, night, weekend). Common for facilities, public safety, dining, and healthcare workers. Typically a percentage of base or flat hourly premium.
Compensation for being available to respond outside normal working hours. Common for IT, facilities, public safety, and residential life staff.
Additional compensation based on years of service. More common at public institutions, especially those under state pay plans. May be a flat amount or percentage per milestone (5, 10, 15 years).

One-time or periodic payment for performance, retention, or market adjustment. Less common in higher ed than private sector but used for hard-to-fill positions, athletic coaches, and senior administrators.
Compensation provided for housing, particularly for university presidents, coaches, or employees required to live on campus (e.g., residence hall directors). May be taxable income.
